texts.preamble: Mariswamy vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Kabc020448272023 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (Scch-23) Dated This The 15th Day Of April - 2025 Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani B.Com. Ll.B (Spl), Xxi Addl. Scj & Acjm Member - Mact, Bengaluru. MVC.No.8683/2023 C/W MVC.No.8684/2023 Petitioner : Sri. Siddesh. K.S, (in Mvc.8683/2023) S/o Shivalingegowda
texts.facts: These claim petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. As both petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment. 2. The common facts leading to the filing of the top noted petitions are that on 20.12.2023 at about 2.00 p.m, when the 3 SCCH-23 MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 petitioner in MVC-8683/2023 being accompanied by two pillion riders (petitioner in MVC-8684/2023 and another by name Shivalinga) was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-E- 1316 near Kamsagara Venkatesh Land, Linganapura, Kamsagara - Chandahalli road, Mandya, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960 came from opposite direction at high speed in a rash & negligent manner and dashed against their motorcycle. Due to the tremendous impact they fell down and sustained grievous injuries. After the accident the petitioners were shifted to Government Hospital, Malavalli, wherein they took first aid and thereafter they were shifted to Venus Multispeciality Hospital, Mysore wherein they took treatment as an inpatient then discharged. They are still under Mariswamy vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45261492/ 2 treatment and have spent considerable amount towards their medicines, conveyance and other incidental expenses. On account of the accidental injuries the petitioners have suffered permanent disablement. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the car and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation. 4 SCCH-23 MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal. Hence he was placed exparte. 4. The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960. However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy. This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident. Negligence on the part of the driver of insured vehicle is denied by this respondent. Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle/ petitioner in MVC.8683/2023 who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident. It is further contended that as per the police documents there are three persons including the injured were traveling on a two wheeler, it amounts to violation of section 128 of the MV Act. In the event of carrying more than one pillion rider on a motorcycle Mariswamy vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45261492/ 3 5 SCCH-23 MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 each one of them was contributed negligence in causing the accident. It is self negligence case as such the claim petition was not maintainable. Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured car did not possess valid & effective DL. Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider. On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him. Further denied all the allegation made in the petition. Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions. 5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues (which are common in both petitions) were framed: ISSUES 1. Ex's .P1 to P13 were marked on his behalf. The petitioner in MVC.No.8684/2023 got examined himself as PW.2. Ex's .P14 to 21 were marked through him. 4 Orthopedics Surgeon was examined as PW.3 (in both the petitions). Ex's .P22 to 25 were marked through this witness. Respondents did not choose to adduce any evidence on their behalf. My findings on the above said issues are as under : Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative (in both the petitions) Issue No.2 (in both the petitions) : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order (in both the petitions) for the following:- 7 SCCH-23 MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 (IN BOTH THE PETITIONS): The evidence on record reveals that one Shashikumar. K.M lodged the complaint about the occurrence of accident with Halagur police. After receipt of the complaint the said police registered an FIR against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MP-0960 and took up investigation. During the course of investigation material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them. The Wound certificates marked at Ex's.P5 and 14 disclose that the petitioners sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
texts.arguments: He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles. Therefore the driver of the car did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle. 9 . During the course of cross-examination of PW's.1 & 2, the learned counsel for insurance company could not elicit anything worthwhile to negate their testimonies. Apart from that perusal of the written statement filed by the respondent No.2 shows that the insurance company has taken divergent stands. At one stretch it has denied the very involvement of its insured vehicle and at another it has contended that there was no negligence on the part of driver of its insured vehicle. Thus, absolutely there is no merit in the defence taken by respondent No.2. The main contention of the insurance company is that the petitioner in MVC.8683/2023 (PW.1) who was riding his motorcycle with two persons on the pillion, has contributed his 9 SCCH-23 MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 Mariswamy vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45261492/ 6 negligence in the occurrence of the accident. However the fact that PW.1 was riding a motorcycle accompanied by two pillion riders, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence. At the most, he would be guilty of being a party to the violation of law. But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence unless it is established that it is the very act of PW.1 riding along with two others contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon him and the other petitioners. 10. In this regard the respondnet No.2 relied the decision reported in 2003 0 Supreme (AP) 1460, in case of United India Insurance Company Limited v/s K. Anjaiah. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Andhra Pradesh held that, in this case admittedly there is triple riding and can be presumed that rider of scooter was discomforted by reason of allowing two pillion riders and thus contributed in causing accident - As such, culpability in causing accident is fixed at 75% on part of driver 10 SCCH-23 MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 of accident lorry and 25% on part of rider of scooter - Appeal, partly allowed. 11. Further the respondent No.2 relied on the decision reported in AIR 2003 Karnataka 258 in the case of P.S. Somaiah and another v/s The Director, Bangalore Diary and others. Wherein it is held that, "(A) Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 1988), S.128 - Driving of Mariswamy vs Ramesh on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45261492/ 7 two - wheelers - Carriage of children in any position in front of rider - Is totally prohibited - State Authorities directed to take steps for enforcement of safety measures - Court also issued clear warning that in case of its failure to do so Court will be required to hold State liable in appropriate cases." 12. Further the respondent No.2 contended that as the petition is not maintainable as the death of or personal injury caused to Workmen in Motor accident arising out of and in court of employment and relied on the decision reported in (2005) 6 SCC 172 in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd., V/s Premabai Patel and others. 11 SCCH-23 MVC.8683/2023 C/w MVC.8684/2023 13. As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mohammed Siddique and another V/s National Insurance Co.Ltd and Others 'There must either be causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim. It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of Law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked'. It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023. Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under : "(b) The accident is of the year 2017. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
